1.explanation: The core of the bug lives in Dropdown.js. The helper `defaultItemToString` and the Dropdown component’s render logic both rely solely on `itemToString(selectedItem)` when setting the toggle button’s `title` attribute and its visible label (`<span>`). When `itemToString` has been overridden to return a React element (via IconDropdown patterns), those places end up stringifying the object (`[object Object]`). To fix this, the Dropdown render function needs to accept a new prop or flag (e.g. `renderSelectedItem`) so that it can use `itemToElement` (or another callback) when rendering the selected item, both for the button content and the `title` attribute, while leaving the menu items alone. PropTypes and defaultProps should be updated alongside the forwardRef render to support this new prop.
1.bug_scenario: In the IconDropdown use case the consumer is hijacking `itemToString` to return a React element (the icon + label) so that the selected item in the closed Dropdown shows the icon. As of v10.43/7.43, the Dropdown’s toggle button `title` attribute still calls `itemToString(selectedItem)`, which in this case returns an object, so you see “title="[object Object]"” on hover instead of the icon or its proper label.

bug_functions: packages/react/src/components/Dropdown/Dropdown.js//(inline render of toggle <button> using itemToString for title and label)
2.explanation: All of the logic that controls how the selected item is rendered lives in the Dropdown component in Dropdown.js. Specifically: 1) the defaultItemToString helper defines how items are converted into strings (used by the title attribute), and 2) the rendering of the toggle <button> always calls itemToString(selectedItem) for both its title prop and label <span>. Because itemToString is being overridden to return React elements, this leads to a bad title string “[object Object]”. To fix this, Dropdown.js must expose a separate API (e.g. a new renderSelectedItem prop) or change the button render logic so that it can use itemToElement for visual content while still calling itemToString for the title tooltip.
2.bug_scenario: The screenshots show a custom IconDropdown built by “hijacking” Dropdown’s itemToString to return a React element so that the selected icon (e.g. a checkmark) renders correctly in the button. Since v10.43 the Dropdown always calls itemToString when setting the button’s title attribute (used as tooltip) and its label <span>. Because itemToString now returns an object (the React element), hovering shows “title=[object Object]” instead of the intended string. The desired behavior is to render the selected item as an element (via itemToElement) but still use a string (via itemToString) for the title/tooltip — or expose a new prop to control which renderer is used for the selected value.
